treatment.logline: A hunted man escapes the market with a metal box, only to discover that the danger has bought him nothing he can understand.

arc.beat: Recognition divides the market into hunter and quarry.
The pursuit compresses from crowded lane to wet alley and iron stairs.
A tank becomes the thin boundary between concealment and discovery.
An empty box replaces the visible pursuer with an unanswered question.

treatment.approach: Play the crime-thriller facet as vulnerable flight, not heroic spectacle: close handheld frames, directional practical light, deep backgrounds and controlled blue, green and sodium colour. Widen only enough to explain pursuit geography. No music and no slow motion. The extra duration belongs to recognition, pursuit coverage, the searching light and the empty-box reaction rather than new events.

treatment.geography: Dinu travels screen left to right; Rohan follows the same direction. The alley opens on the right of the market; the iron stairs rise toward screen right. On the roof Dinu crouches on the camera side of a water tank; Rohan searches its far side and continues right. All coverage stays on this side of the pursuit axis. Dinu carries the box under his jacket against his left ribs with his left hand; Rohan retains the torch in his right hand throughout.
treatment.key_image: A narrow torch beam crosses the tank above Dinu's compressed body; later the same dark shelter contains a visibly empty metal box.
advice: Let Rohan's recognition register before L1 and before the running.
Cut on the cart impact and the slipping foot, not on arbitrary motion.
The cart incident is fragmented into a physical cause, the cart tipping and the pursuit beyond it; no bodies make contact.
Keep the empty interior readable before returning to Dinu for L6.

editor_notes: The must bin contains 15 clips, 78 seconds of takes; use it as raw material, not a binding 78-second assembly. The intended scene runs approximately 75 seconds, paced with the recognition, search, empty interior and final reaction.
The lane master and Rohan recognition single establish geography before the L1 performing single. Keep left-to-right pursuit and Rohan's opposing initial eyeline consistent.

The cart contact, cart-tip detail and pursuit master are consecutive pieces of the same event. Match the upper rail across the impact cut and open the pursuit master on the already tipped cart and scattered oranges. Use soft foreground occlusions and sound to suggest passage through shoppers without requiring body contact or sharp crowds.

The alley entry, slip/recovery and stair master are consecutive parts of the pursuit, not alternate performances of one long move. Match Dinu's box at his left ribs and Rohan's torch in his right hand.

On the roof, match the torch patch from the search across the tank to Dinu's reaction, then let footsteps recede. The box is already in Dinu's lap at the opening detail; the edit skips the extraction, not the opening. Keep the empty interior unobstructed and let L6 follow on the face.

The checker flags fast-hand feasibility on the two running shots. Neither asks for finger work: the box and torch remain in fixed grips; favour the faces and bodies if a render introduces finger motion.
The short cart and pursuit shots have half-second handles. Use their impacts and continuous direction as match points; do not trim L1 or L6.

Speed ramps, freeze frames, digital punch-ins and split screens are post-only; clean sources are supplied, but none is required in the reference cut. Avoid slow motion, mirrors, intricate finger work and contact between bodies. Music is omitted; rain, breath, impacts and footsteps lead.

editor_notes: The must bin contains 15 clips, 78 seconds of takes; use it as raw material, not a binding 78-second assembly. The intended scene runs approximately 75 seconds, paced with the recognition, search, empty interior and final reaction.
The lane master and Rohan recognition single establish geography before the L1 performing single. Keep left-to-right pursuit and Rohan's opposing initial eyeline consistent.

The cart contact, cart-tip detail and pursuit master are consecutive pieces of the same event. Match the upper rail across the impact cut and open the pursuit master on the already tipped cart and scattered oranges. Use soft foreground occlusions and sound to suggest passage through shoppers without requiring body contact or sharp crowds.

The alley entry, slip/recovery and stair master are consecutive parts of the pursuit, not alternate performances of one long move. Match Dinu's box at his left ribs and Rohan's torch in his right hand.

On the roof, match the torch patch from the search across the tank to Dinu's reaction, then let footsteps recede. The box is already in Dinu's lap at the opening detail; the edit skips the extraction, not the opening. Keep the empty interior unobstructed and let L6 follow on the face.

The checker flags fast-hand feasibility on the two running shots. Neither asks for finger work: the box and torch remain in fixed grips; favour the faces and bodies if a render introduces finger motion.
The short cart and pursuit shots have half-second handles. Use their impacts and continuous direction as match points; do not trim L1 or L6.

Speed ramps, freeze frames, digital punch-ins and split screens are post-only; clean sources are supplied, but none is required in the reference cut. Avoid slow motion, mirrors, intricate finger work and contact between bodies. Music is omitted; rain, breath, impacts and footsteps lead.
blend_notes: c16 — After c14 reveals the empty interior, hold Dinu’s isolated reaction over rooftop rain and his breathing; then return to c15 for L6.
c17 — Cut into c12 at the paused beam, over Rohan’s rooftop footsteps and rain; return to c12 as the search moves on.
c18 — After c15 completes L6, retreat from Dinu over rooftop rain and distant market ambience; no music.
c19 — After c07’s pursuit passage, hold briefly on the settling oranges over receding running footsteps and market rain, then cut to the alley.
c20 — Open moment 1 before c01 and c02, using market rain and foot traffic; retain the established left-to-right pursuit axis.

review.why: A rainy wide reveal establishes the distance across the lane before the recognition singles.
Rohan’s readable performing single carries the immediate impact of L1; a cutaway would dilute it.
A ground-level aftermath of the oranges gives the cart disruption a distinct visual consequence without repeating its tip.
The locked alley entry, slip and recovery, and stair master already explain the route and near loss of balance.
A tank-surface insert makes the searching beam’s pause and departure tactile without duplicating the held reaction.
An isolated facial reaction registers the empty box after the locked opening insert.
A restrained crane retreat leaves Dinu small in the rooftop shelter after L6.
